questions.question: Compare the properties of metals and solid non-metals.
questions.expected_answer: Metals are shiny, hard and strong, malleable and ductile, have high melting points and conduct heat and electricity well. Solid non-metals, like carbon and sulfur, are dull and brittle, cannot be hammered or drawn into wire, and most do not conduct heat or electricity well.

questions.question: Explain the difference between rusting and tarnishing, and name the magnetic metals.
questions.expected_answer: Only iron and steel rust, when water and oxygen reach them; rust is orange-brown, flaky and weakens the metal. Other metals, like silver and copper, tarnish: the surface goes dull or changes colour and can be polished off. The magnetic metals are iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

questions.question: Name the five ways of combining materials, with one example each, and three properties that make processed materials useful.
questions.expected_answer: Mix and set: concrete or plaster of Paris. Mix: glue paste. Mix and cook: bread. Mix and cool: jelly. Mix, dry and fire: clay bricks. Processed materials can be strong, durable, waterproof, fire resistant, colourful or textured.
